arxiv-1811-09570.title: A Survey on Synchrophasor Data Quality and Cybersecurity Challenges, and Evaluation of their Interdependencies
arxiv-1811-09570.creator: Aditya Sundararajan, Tanwir Khan, Amir Moghadasi, Arif I. Sarwat
arxiv-1811-09570.description: Abstract Synchrophasor devices guarantee situation awareness for real-time monitoring and operational visibility of the smart grid. With their widespread implementation, significant challenges have emerged, especially in communication, data quality and cybersecurity. The existing literature treats these challenges as separate problems, when in reality, they have a complex interplay.

arxiv-2205-03796.creator: Christos A. Athanasiadis, Katerina Kalampogia-Evangelinou
arxiv-2205-03796.description: Abstract . The coefficients of the chain polynomial of a finite poset enumerate chains in the poset by their number of elements. The chain polynomials of the partition lattices and their standard type B B analogues are shown to have only real roots.

arxiv-2211-07603.title: Problem Classification for Tailored Helpdesk Auto-Replies
arxiv-2211-07603.creator: Reece Nicholls, Ryan Fellows, Steve Battle, and Hisham Ihshaish
arxiv-2211-07603.description: Abstract IT helpdesks are charged with the task of responding quickly to user queries. To give the user confidence that their query matters, the helpdesk will auto-reply to the user with confirmation that their query has been received and logged. This auto-reply may include generic ‘boiler-plate’ text that addresses common problems of the day, with relevant information and links.

arxiv-2501-16043.title: Smoothing properties of the Wilson flow and the topological charge
arxiv-2501-16043.creator: J. Tobias Tsang
arxiv-2501-16043.description: Abstract We study SU ( N C ) (N_{C}) gauge theories with a single fermion in the two-index antisymmetric representation to predict the mesonic spectrum of supersymmetric 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 SYM theories. Using gradient flow methods, we investigate fractional topological charges in N C = 4 N_{C}=4 ensembles with varying lattice spacings.

arxiv-2506-21356.title: ShotBench: Expert-Level Cinematic Understanding in Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2506-21356.creator: Hongbo Liu Jingwen He Yi Jin Dian Zheng, Yuhao Dong Fan Zhang Ziqi Huang Yinan He Yangguang Li, Weichao Chen Yu Qiao Wanli Ouyang Shengjie Zhao Ziwei Liu
arxiv-2506-21356.description: Abstract Cinematography, the fundamental visual language of film, is essential for conveying narrative, emotion, and aesthetic quality. While recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate strong general visual understanding, their proficiency in comprehending the nuanced cinematic grammar embedded within individual shots remains largely unexplored and lacks robust evaluation.

arxiv-2507-04864.title: Music Boomerang: Reusing Diffusion Models for Data Augmentation and Audio Manipulation
arxiv-2507-04864.creator: Alexander Fichtinger, Jan Schlüter ( 0000-0003-3862-6888 ), Gerhard Widmer ( 0000-0003-3531-1282 )
arxiv-2507-04864.description: Abstract Generative models of music audio are typically used to generate output based solely on a text prompt or melody. Boomerang sampling, recently proposed for the image domain, allows generating output close to an existing example, using any pretrained diffusion model.

arxiv-2510-04727.title: Directional Sheaf Hypergraph Networks: Unifying Learning on Directed and Undirected Hypergraphs
arxiv-2510-04727.creator: Emanuele Mule, Stefano Fiorini, Antonio Purificato, Federico Siciliano, Stefano Coniglio, Fabrizio Silvestri
arxiv-2510-04727.description: Abstract Hypergraphs provide a natural way to represent higher-order interactions among multiple entities. While undirected hypergraphs have been extensively studied, the case of directed hypergraphs, which can model oriented group interactions, remains largely under-explored despite its relevance for many applications. Recent approaches in this direction often exhibit an implicit bias toward homophily, which limits their effectiveness in heterophilic settings.

pmc-10495464.title: Sex and menstrual cycle influence human spatial navigation strategies and performance
pmc-10495464.creator: Alana Brown, Ford Burles, Giuseppe Iaria, Gillian Einstein, Morris Moscovitch
pmc-10495464.description: Which facets of human spatial navigation do sex and menstrual cycle influence? To answer this question, a cross-sectional online study of reproductive age women and men was conducted in which participants were asked to demonstrate and self-report their spatial navigation skills and strategies.

pmc-10649971.creator: Qingjie Wang, Shiyuan Xu, Lei Zhong, Xiya Zhao, Li Wang, Ryszard Lobinski
pmc-10649971.description: Ginkgo biloba is a highly valuable medicinal plant known for its rich secondary metabolites, including flavonoids. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) can be used as nanofertilizers and nano-growth regulators to promote plant growth and development. However, little is known about the effects of ZnO-NPs on flavonoids in G. biloba. In this study, G.

pmc-11432219.title: Epidemiological and Prognostic Importance of New-Onset Cancer as a Net Adverse Clinical Outcome after ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction
pmc-11432219.creator: Toshiharu Fujii, Yuji Ikari, Aleš Blinc
pmc-11432219.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The study assessed the epidemiological frequency and prognostic impact of new-onset cancer as an additional net adverse clinical outcome in patients after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), considering its potential clinical significance alongside classical endpoints. This study was designed as a single-center observational study, including 1285 consecutive patients who were diagnosed as STEMI patients as the subject, and the frequency and prognosis of new-onset cancer after STEMI onset were assessed.

pmc-11470781.title: Sexual dimorphism and allometry in human scapula shape
pmc-11470781.creator: Erin C S Lee, Rebekah L Lawrence, Michael J Rainbow
pmc-11470781.description: Scapula shape is highly variable across humans and appears to be sexually dimorphic—differing significantly between biological males and females. However, previous investigations of sexual dimorphism in scapula shape have not considered the effects of allometry (the relationship between size and shape).

pmc-11494259.title: Applying Implementation Science to Advance Electronic Health Record–Driven Learning Health Systems: Case Studies, Challenges, and Recommendations
pmc-11494259.creator: Katy E Trinkley, Anna M Maw, Cristina Huebner Torres, Amy G Huebschmann, Russell E Glasgow, Guy Tsafnat, Sarah Greene, Taylor Watterson
pmc-11494259.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). With the widespread implementation of electronic health records (EHRs), there has been significant progress in developing learning health systems (LHSs) aimed at improving health and health care delivery through rapid and continuous knowledge generation and translation. To support LHSs in achieving these goals, implementation science (IS) and its frameworks are increasingly being leveraged to ensure that LHSs are feasible, rapid, iterative, reliable, reproducible, equitable, and sustainable.

pmc-12557643.title: Our technique of combined full thoracoscopic (no access incision) and posterior midline approach for en bloc resection of non-small cell lung cancer invading the spine: tips and tricks
pmc-12557643.creator: Madalina Grigoroiu, Emmanuel Brian, Alessio Mariolo, Christian Mazel, Sebastien Moreau
pmc-12557643.description: En bloc resection of lung cancers invading the vertebral column remains a major challenge for both surgeons and patients. At Montsouris Mutualiste Institut, we have a nearly 30-year history of surgically treating such cases. With the development of minimally invasive technology, our technique has also evolved over the time.

pmc-12986564.title: An Infant Formula with Partially Hydrolyzed Whey and Intact Protein Demonstrates Adequate Growth and Safety: A 6-Month Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial
pmc-12986564.creator: Qianqian Shen, Hua Jiang, Shuai Mao, Sha Luo, Yanjie Hao, Wenxin Liang, Tingchao He, Lotte Neergaard Jacobsen, Nan Sheng, Jing Yin, Xiaoying Feng, Xiaojiang Jia, Yvan Vandenplas, Yumei Zhang
pmc-12986564.description: Background/Objectives: Evidence suggests that partially hydrolyzed whey protein promotes appropriate infant growth; however, research on its long-term effects, especially in Asia, remains limited. This study set out to evaluate the effects of an infant formula containing partially hydrolyzed whey and intact protein on infant growth and development.

pmc-13292208.title: KNexPHENIX: A PHENIX-Based Workflow for Improving Cryo-EM and Crystallographic Structural Models
pmc-13292208.creator: Suparno Nandi, Graeme L. Conn
pmc-13292208.description: New and improved methods for visualizing complex macromolecules in atomic detail continue to expand structural information in the Protein Data Bank but accurately refining atomic models from experimental maps remains a challenge due to efficiency limitations of current refinement approaches.

pmc-7619686.title: How to Elicit Thought Disorder During Clinical Interviews: A Practical Guide
pmc-7619686.creator: Lena Palaniyappan, Oliver Delgaram-Nejad, Eric YH Chen
pmc-7619686.description: The reliable assessment of Formal Thought Disorder (FTD), a collection of observable signs of suspected thinking dysfunction, is the cornerstone of interviewing a person with psychosis. A significant gap persists between the success of reliable assessments reported in published rating scales of FTD and the practical constraints of a clinical interview.
